articles.title: Natural history of solitary osteochondroma : a retrospective analysis of 236 patients in South Korea.
articles.authors: Sung MJ, Kim CH, Jung ST, Kim S
articles.outcomes: Spontaneous regression rates, tumour progression, surgical intervention rates, recurrence rates, predictors of regression
articles.take_home: Osteochondromas behave very differently depending on skeletal maturity. Younger patients (especially under 14.8 years) frequently experience spontaneous regression without surgery, particularly if the tumour is in the upper arm, whereas skeletally mature patients have more stable disease but more often need surgery.

articles.title: Superior Internal Rotation after Anatomic vs. Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty Performed with Lesser Tuberosity Osteotomy.
articles.authors: Shi BY, Fiandeiro M, Satalich JR, Saha I, Uvarov E, Chhabra V, et al.
articles.population: Patients with glenohumeral arthritis and intact rotator cuff undergoing shoulder replacement
articles.sample_size: 206 patients (46 reverse, 160 anatomic) with minimum 2-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: Internal rotation, external rotation, range of motion, SANE score, ASES score, anterior shoulder pain and dysfunction, pain severity
articles.take_home: When both types of shoulder replacement used the same technique to reattach the subscapularis muscle, anatomic replacements gave better internal rotation movement than reverse replacements. This suggests the advantage comes from how the implant itself works rather than how the muscle is repaired.

articles.title: Assessing the Usefulness of Diagnostic Shoulder Arthroscopy in Evaluating Painful Shoulder Replacement: A Retrospective Case Series.
articles.authors: Lazzara JT, Nwadike BA, Ofori-Kuragu AG, Otto RJ
articles.population: Adults with persistent pain after total or reverse shoulder replacement with inconclusive standard tests
articles.sample_size: 29 patients (25 reverse shoulder arthroplasty, 4 total shoulder arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Diagnostic shoulder arthroscopy identified mechanical problems in 51.7% of patients, infection in 17.2%, and no abnormalities in 41.4%. Findings guided treatment decisions in 44.8% of patients who underwent revision surgery.
articles.take_home: Diagnostic shoulder arthroscopy can help identify hidden causes of pain after shoulder replacement when standard imaging and tests are inconclusive, including wear, impingement, infection, or no detectable problem. This information can guide whether patients need further surgery or non-surgical treatment.

articles.title: Shoulder Injury and Surgery Patterns Among Astronauts Across Spaceflight Phases and Mission Operations: An Analysis of 677 Injuries from 1981 to 2024.
articles.authors: Ward GH, Jacobs SA, Marrero AN, Scheuring RA, Anderson DN
articles.sample_size: 677 shoulder injuries from astronauts between 1981 and 2024
articles.outcomes: Prevalence and distribution of shoulder injuries and surgeries across spaceflight phases; association between training exposure and injury timing; most common diagnoses (tendinopathy, osteoarthritis, rotator cuff injury) and surgical procedures (rotator cuff repair, arthroscopic debridement)
articles.take_home: Astronauts experienced more shoulder injuries after spaceflight than before or during it, and those who spent six months or more in microgravity were injured sooner after returning to Earth. More intensive training in the underwater facility before flight was linked to earlier shoulder problems, suggesting that training stress may contribute to injury risk.

articles.title: Total Shoulder Arthroplasty and Scapulohumeral Rhythm: The clinical impact of achieving native shoulder mechanics.
articles.authors: Khawaja SR, Hardrick JC, Und Aspang JS, Bailey E, Sinha M, Gunawardana K, et al.
articles.population: Patients who had total shoulder arthroplasty (anatomic or reverse) with minimum 12 months follow-up
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported pain (VAS), shoulder function (SANE and ASES scores), and scapulohumeral rhythm measurements
articles.take_home: Patients with lower scapulohumeral rhythm (more scapular movement relative to arm movement) after shoulder replacement had higher pain and worse function. Achieving shoulder mechanics closer to a normal native shoulder may lead to better pain relief and function after shoulder replacement surgery.

articles.title: Infraspinatus Advancement via Remplissage Improves Dynamic Anterior Stability but Reduces External Rotation Moment Arm: A Computational Study.
articles.authors: Wang S, Danelson K, Habet N, Trasolini NA, Waterman BR, Reynolds AW
articles.population: Shoulder models based on 16 shoulders with Hill-Sachs lesions
articles.outcomes: Infraspinatus posterior force vector, external rotation moment arm, and abduction moment arm at different degrees of tendon advancement
articles.take_home: Adding the infraspinatus muscle to remplissage surgery improves shoulder stability by increasing the force pushing the arm bone back into place, but this comes at a cost of reduced ability to rotate the shoulder outwards. Surgeons need to balance these benefits and drawbacks when deciding how much to advance the muscle during surgery.

articles.title: Short Term Results of Structural Bone Grafting of Glenoid Defects in Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review/Meta-analysis of Implant Design and Graft Characteristics.
articles.authors: Penvose I, Toavs T, Covarrubias O, Chang K, Daher M, Molino J, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty with glenoid bone defects
articles.outcomes: Bone graft incorporation rates, glenoid baseplate loosening rates, and revision surgery rates
articles.take_home: Both autograft and allograft bone grafts incorporate successfully in over 94 percent of cases when used to rebuild the shoulder socket in reverse shoulder replacement surgery. However, revision surgeries (where the implant is replaced a second time) have higher rates of baseplate loosening and may need further surgery compared to first-time operations.

articles.title: Quality and Rate of Recovery after Simpliciti Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty and Tornier Pyrocarbon Hemiarthroplasty: A Propensity Score-Matched Comparative Study.
articles.authors: Hatzidakis AM, Mauter L, Rossington AK, Venegoni M, Tashjian RZ
articles.population: Younger patients with glenohumeral osteoarthritis undergoing shoulder surgery
articles.sample_size: 74 patients in each group (148 total after matching)
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeon scores, Constant scores, pain scores, and minimal clinically important difference achievement at 3, 6, and 24 months
articles.take_home: Both types of shoulder replacement surgery produced similar results for osteoarthritis over two years. The anatomic total shoulder replacement showed slightly less pain at 6 and 24 months, but the difference was less than 1 point and unlikely to matter to patients in practice.

articles.title: Kinesiotaping effects in patients with rotator cuff-related shoulder pain: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Del Blanco-Muniz A, Sanchez-Sierra A, Mares-Herranz A, Zubia-Raez A, Merino-Andres J
articles.population: Patients with rotator cuff-related shoulder pain
articles.outcomes: Pain, shoulder function, range of motion
articles.take_home: Kinesiotaping provides only small short-term improvements in shoulder function and pain during activity, with unclear effects on range of motion. It should be used alongside, not instead of, exercise-based rehabilitation and education.

articles.title: An International Expert Consensus Statement Defining the Best Practices and Areas of Uncertainty Concerning the Use of Orthobiologics.
articles.authors: Kunze KN, Morgan JT, Gerhold C, Nishioka T, Piuzzi NS, Chahla J
articles.population: 24-member international expert panel in orthopaedic medicine
articles.outcomes: 62 consensus statements on orthobiologics use, with 96.8% achieving agreement; high consensus on PRP for various conditions, bone marrow concentrate, and other biologics; lower consensus on rotator cuff repair and cell-based therapies
articles.take_home: Experts largely agreed on when and how to use various biologic treatments in orthopaedics, but identified significant gaps in understanding about how to prepare these treatments, what doses to use, and how well they actually work in specific situations. The field needs better standardisation of methods and quality control.

articles.title: Can Total Elbow Arthroplasty Effectively Treat Post-traumatic Sequelae After Proximal Ulna or Radius Fracture and Fracture-Dislocations?
articles.authors: You DZ, Rudisill SS, Fossum BW, Baird MD, O' Driscoll SW, Sanchez-Sotelo J, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent total elbow arthroplasty for post-traumatic complications after proximal ulna or radius fractures or fracture-dislocations
articles.sample_size: 40 elbows (mean age 59 years, 58% female, mean follow-up 9 years)
articles.outcomes: Implant survival at 10 years: 73% free from any revision or resection, 83% free from mechanical failure or radiographic loosening, 88% free from infection-related revision. Revision rate 28%. Common complications: neurologic (20%), aseptic loosening (18%), deep infection (13%).
articles.take_home: Total elbow replacement can provide good pain relief and function for people with post-traumatic elbow problems after complex fractures, with 73% of implants surviving 10 years without needing revision surgery. However, these operations are technically challenging and carry meaningful risks of complications, particularly nerve problems and infection.

articles.title: Proximal Humerus Fractures Treated with Single or Dual-Plate Constructs: A Comparison of Clinical Outcomes.
articles.authors: Sogbein OA, Klas P, Di Michele J, Case C, Henry PDG, Sheth U, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18 and over with proximal humerus fractures treated with open reduction internal fixation
articles.outcomes: Complications including varus cutout and non-union, reoperation rates, and mechanical failures
articles.take_home: Patients treated with dual-plate fixation had significantly fewer reoperations (5.4% versus 22.7%) and lower rates of varus cutout and non-union compared to single-plate fixation, with no increase in other complications. Dual-plate fixation may be particularly beneficial for fractures caused by high-energy injuries.

articles.title: Effects of neurocognitive reactive activities on upper extremity closed kinetic chain functional performance testing.
articles.authors: Stoddard SM, Lewis K, Riemann BL, Davies GJ
articles.outcomes: Test-retest reliability of upper extremity functional performance tests with and without neurocognitive reactive components, measured by intraclass correlation coefficients, number of touches, and reaction time
articles.take_home: Two new versions of an upper extremity stability test that include mental reaction tasks showed reasonable reliability and produced different results compared to the standard test. These cognitive versions may help doctors make better decisions about when athletes can return to sport, though more research is needed to confirm they are useful in real-world settings.

articles.title: Assessment of "Spin" in the abstracts of systematic reviews in leading upper extremity surgery journals over the past 10 years: A cross-sectional methodological study.
articles.authors: Balogun OT, Jain V, Sritharan P, Param A, Shah A, Lameire DL, et al.
articles.population: Systematic reviews published in leading upper extremity surgery journals
articles.outcomes: Prevalence and types of spin (misleading reporting) in systematic review abstracts, assessed using a 9-type framework
articles.take_home: Over half of systematic reviews in leading upper extremity surgery journals contained misleading reporting in their abstracts, most commonly by claiming benefits despite high risk of bias. This suggests readers should be cautious when interpreting these reviews for clinical practice.

articles.title: Comparative functional outcomes of arthroscopic versus mini-open rotator cuff repair: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Llombart-Blanco R, Mariscal G, Zabady AH, Broqua P, Barrios C, Llombart-Ais R
articles.population: Adults undergoing rotator cuff repair surgery
articles.outcomes: Functional scores (ASES, Constant-Murley, DASH), range of motion, and pain (VAS)
articles.take_home: Arthroscopic and mini-open rotator cuff repair surgery produce similar results for function, pain relief and movement up to two years after surgery. Both techniques appear equally effective, so the choice between them may depend on other factors such as surgeon preference and patient circumstances.

articles.title: Region-specific evaluation of Hounsfield units on elbow CT as a predictor of osteoporosis in patients at risk.
articles.authors: Klingler F, Schmid C, Muhlenfeld N, Jung M, Bogner B, Knoblauch AL, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent both elbow CT scan and DXA scan within two years
articles.outcomes: Correlation between Hounsfield units on elbow CT and DXA measurements; discriminatory capacity of HU measurements for detecting osteoporosis using area under ROC curve
articles.take_home: Measurements of bone density from standard elbow CT scans can help identify osteoporosis, with the ulnar notch area being particularly accurate. This could help surgeons assess bone quality when DXA scans are not available before emergency trauma surgery.

articles.title: Lower Postoperative Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index Is Associated with Increased Complications and Reoperations Following Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Polam V, Stokes L, Sauvanell YM, Gosselin M, Nahr A, Denard PJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing total shoulder arthroplasty (anatomic or reverse)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications, reoperations, range of motion, patient-reported outcomes (ASES, VAS pain, WOOS, SANE), and patient satisfaction
articles.take_home: Patients with poor nutritional status after shoulder replacement surgery (measured by a blood test called GNRI) had significantly higher rates of complications and needed repeat surgery more often, though their long-term pain relief and movement improved similarly to well-nourished patients. Checking nutritional status after surgery might help identify patients at higher risk of problems.

articles.title: Does Teres Minor Trophicity Affect Outcomes After Arthroscopically-Assisted Lower Trapezius Tendon Transfer in Irreparable Posterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears?
articles.authors: Baek CH, Kim BT, Kim JG, Lim C, Kim SJ
articles.population: Patients with irreparable posterosuperior rotator cuff tears undergoing arthroscopically-assisted lower trapezius tendon transfer
articles.sample_size: 104 patients (19 hypertrophic teres minor, 72 normal, 13 hypotrophic)
articles.outcomes: Pain (VAS), function (Constant and ASES scores), range of motion, complications, and retear rates at mean 45 months follow-up
articles.take_home: The size of the teres minor muscle before surgery did not affect how well patients recovered after lower trapezius tendon transfer, with all groups showing significant improvements in pain, shoulder movement, and function. Complication rates were similar regardless of teres minor size.

articles.title: Tracer uptake pattern around the scapula after reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: stress analysis using single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography imaging.
articles.authors: Cho CH, Son ES, Kim SG, Yoon JP, Won KS, Kim DH
articles.study_type: Retrospective observational study with prospective clinical follow-up
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Tracer uptake patterns on SPECT/CT imaging at 6 months postoperatively; stress fractures and stress reactions; correlation between tracer uptake values and clinical parameters including pain, function, and shoulder movement
articles.take_home: After reverse shoulder replacement, imaging showed increased stress around the shoulder blade, particularly at the back of the shoulder bone, and three patients developed stress fractures or stress reactions. The study suggests that special imaging scans might help identify patients at risk of these stress-related problems.
